Hi Tom,
Thanks for your question, nice to hear from you.
There's two ways that marine mammals hydrate themselves. First is that they just eat water or actually eat preys that are very high in water content. So a whale eats a ton of krill, for example, and the krill are very high in water, and that's actually where most of their hydration comes from. For those of them that drink water directly, that's actually a problem because seawater has a very high salt concentration. And in order to drink seawater and actually hydrate, they have to separate the salt from the water somehow. So all marine mammals have very efficient kidneys that can remove very high amounts of salt. Some of them also have dedicated salt glands. For example, seals have these nasal glands where they just cry out the salt. And for some birds, that's also very common, they have these glands next to their beaks. So basically, they hydrate themselves in two ways. One, by eating very water rich prey, and two by drinking seawater or brackish water, and then removing the salt, the salt from the water either through their kidneys or through salt glands.
Anyway, let's meet soon, want to meet you. Cheers.
